thread:
maya: Quick sync request — we need to finalize the spec for a "rollforward" migration path vs keeping long-lived pins for customers. TL;DR: propose a default auto-rollforward with opt-out pins + a gated exception flow for long-tail enterprise customers. Thoughts?

jordan: +1 to default auto-rollforward. We keep seeing ops overhead from manual pinning. But need concrete guardrails for quality.

eli: Agree on defaults. What are the acceptance criteria for auto-rollforward? Are we requiring eval parity + perf checks?

maya: My draft acceptance criteria: 1) pass canonical eval suite (>= baseline F1/ROUGE delta threshold), 2) 95th pct latency within 1.3x of pinned model, 3) no >2% regression on key prompts (customer-specified testset), 4) rollback path & canary for 24h.

katie: Sounds reasonable. Add cost delta threshold (e.g., per-token cost increase <= 10%) — infra will push back if cost explodes for hosted customers.

sam: For Dedicated/Private customers we need explicit opt-in to auto-rollforward. They often require audit logs and change windows. Maybe default auto-rollforward for Hosted only, with a migration proposal for Dedicated.

maya: Yep. Hosted = auto-rollforward by default with a 14-day post-roll grace window where previous version is still accessible via a compatibility shim (read-only). Dedicated/Private = manual unless customer opts in.

eli: Operational flow idea: preflight job that runs on a staging traffic sample and a 1% canary for 6 hours. If metrics pass, rollout in phases: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated watch-dog checks and pause on anomalies.

maya: I sketched a checklist for the preflight. Posting here:

```
Preflight checklist:
- Eval suite: unit + regen + customer-critical prompts
- Perf: 95th latency, p50 token rate, GPU memory check
- Cost: unit cost delta
- Safety: safety-checker pass + no new toxic outputs on seeded prompts
- Compatibility: API/response format regression tests
- Observability: dashboards, alert thresholds, tracing hooks enabled
- Canary policy: 1% for 6h, auto-rollback on alert
```

katie: Can we automate the eval suite run and post results to a PR comment? That will make product sign-off faster.

sam: +1. Also add a customer-communication template for enterprise customers — legal wants 7d notice for breaking changes.

jordan: Edge case: if a model is quantized and the new one is not, we might see latency improvements but quality regressions. Need model-profile metadata to drive decision.

maya: Good point. Adding model profile gating: quantization flags, expected tokenization differences, and recommended kernel profiles. If major profile drift, require manual QA.

eli: Who owns the final decision? Product signs off on customer-facing risks, Research/Applied ML signs off on evals, Eng Infra signs off on perf/cost. Need a clear sign-off checklist itemized in the PR.

maya: Proposed owners: Product (maya/katie) = customer risk sign-off; Research (eli) = quality sign-off; Eng Infra (sam) = perf/cost sign-off; Ops (jordan) = rollout ops. If any owner vetoes, migration goes to exception lane.

sam: For the exception lane, we should define SLAs: timeline for manual migration assistance, length of pin grace period, and billing implications. My suggestion: 90-day standard pin grace unless contract specifies otherwise.

katie: 90 days is fine but we need an escalation matrix for customers asking for longer pins. Legal has to sign off on >180 days.

maya: I can draft the migration policy doc with these numbers and a customer comms template. Action: maya to send PR w/ checklist + rollout automation tickets.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: New workflow created: "catalog-rollforward-preflight". Runs: evals, perf-check, safety-scan. Trigger: PR to model-catalog with label `rollforward-request`.

jordan: Nice — can we add a slack notif to #customer-success when the canary hits 25%? They should monitor support spikes.

maya: Yes, will add that to workflow. Also adding a quick opt-out API for customers: POST /catalog/v1/models/{model_id}/pin with body {"expires_at": "2026-06-01", "reason": "contract request"}.

eli: One more ask: include a "quality smoke" metric that runs a small set of user-provided prompts (if customer provided them) in preflight. If any fail, require explicit approval.

sam: Agree. That helps catch functional regressions.

katie: Timeline? Can we aim to have the automation + policy doc ready for 2-week sprint review?

maya: Target: PR + automation proof-of-concept by EOD sprint-2 (14 days). I'll own doc + PR. @eli to own eval infra changes; @sam to own workflow integration; @katie to review customer comms/legal hooks.

jordan: I'll set up the canary dashboard and add alert runbooks to eng-oncall.

maya: OK — if no blockers, I'll spin the PR and schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow to walk through. Thanks all :tada:
